obligation: USCG Cybersecurity in the Marine Transportation System final rule
basis: 101.605(a) reaches owners and operators of U.S.-flagged vessels, facilities and OCS facilities required to have a security plan under 33 CFR parts 104 to 106. All operations are onshore in Florida and Alabama; the company owns no vessel, waterfront facility or OCS facility

The directive applies to owners and operators of hazardous liquid and natural gas pipelines that TSA has notified are critical. The company operates a 92-mile crude gathering system, so a notice is possible; General Counsel confirmed in P03 fieldwork that none has been received

Not a final rule. As proposed, 226.2 reaches entities above the SBA size standard or meeting a sector criterion: 850 employees is below the 1,250-employee standard for NAICS 211120 (13 CFR 121.201), and no MTSA, TSA-identified pipeline or NERC CIP criterion is met

obligation: Part 195 regulated rural gathering line requirements
basis: 195.11(a): an 8-inch onshore gathering line in a rural area within one-quarter mile of a drinking water unusually sensitive area, operating above 20% of specified minimum yield strength. The 195.11(b) requirements (MOP, operator qualification, Subpart B reporting, record retention under 195.11(d) and others) apply

obligation: Part 195 reporting requirements for other gathering lines
basis: Gathering lines that are not regulated rural gathering lines must meet the Subpart B annual, accident and safety-related condition reporting requirements, except the telephone notice in 195.52 (195.15(c)(2))

obligation: Control room management and procedural manual
basis: 195.11(b) does not list 195.446 or 195.402 for regulated rural gathering lines, and the lines are not transmission lines. The company applies alarm review, shift handover and emergency procedures voluntarily

obligation: Part 195 exclusions for production facilities and tank trucks
basis: Well-to-battery flow lines are production facilities, and South Florida and Alabama crude leaves by purchaser tank trucks

obligation: NIST CSF 2.0 with NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3
basis: No binding federal sector cyber rule applies (N21-R01 to N21-R03). The company used the same benchmark for its 2024 review

obligation: Oil discharge notice to the National Response Center
basis: The company stores and moves crude at tank batteries, flow lines and the gathering system; a discharge that reaches water must be reported. The emergency response plan covers spill and release reporting

The company is a covered entity holding personal information of royalty owners (Social Security or taxpayer numbers, bank accounts) and 850 employees (Social Security, driver license and health plan numbers)
Subsection (8) covers customer records, and the company has no consumer customers (501.171(1)(c))
Royalty owners live in more than 40 states; the law of each state where affected individuals reside applies, confirmed by counsel at the time of an incident

obligation: Gathering agreements and the largest shipper's SOC 2 request
basis: The agreements carry measurement, statement and confidentiality duties; the largest shipper asks for a SOC 2 Type 2 report on gathering and measurement services
The policy requires MFA on all remote access and notice to the carrier; panel firms are named
Applies to all U.S. persons
No offshore or OCS operations
MSHA issues no cybersecurity rules; the company operates oil wells, not mines
The company holds no SSI: it has no MTSA facility and no TSA-notified pipeline
No EAR-controlled technology identified in the vendor list or purchasing records
The contract register shows no federal contracts or subcontracts
Privately held; files no SEC reports

obligation: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
basis: The company does not accept payment cards; revenue is crude, gas and gathering sales
